scheme_name: Cycle Scheme for the Children of Construction Workers (P.B.O.C.W.W.B)
description:
The Cycle Scheme for the Children of Construction Workers is a welfare initiative launched by the Government of India to support the education and mobility of children whose parents are engaged in the construction industry.

This scheme was officially launched on 1st June 2018 under the aegis of the Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide bicycles to children of construction workers to facilitate their commute to educational institutions.

The initiative aims to enhance the educational opportunities for these children by ensuring they have a reliable mode of transport.

The scheme specifically targets children aged between 5 to 18 years who are enrolled in schools.

The government aims to distribute bicycles to approximately 50,000 children under this scheme annually.

Each bicycle provided under this scheme has an estimated cost of INR 2,500.

The total budget allocated for the implementation of this scheme is around INR 125 crores for the year 2023-2024.

The eligibility criteria for beneficiaries include being a child of a registered construction worker.

The construction worker must be registered with the Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The family income of the construction worker should not exceed INR 3 lakhs per annum.

The children must be studying in recognized schools, either government or private.

The application process involves several steps to ensure transparency and accountability.

First, the applicant must fill out the prescribed application form available at local welfare board offices.

The application form requires details such as the name of the child, age, school name, and the registration number of the construction worker.

Applicants must submit proof of the construction worker's registration with the welfare board.

Additionally, they must provide a copy of the child's school admission or attendance certificate.

The completed application form along with the required documents must be submitted to the local office of the Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

After submission, the applications are verified by the concerned authorities.

The verification process typically takes around 30 days from the date of application submission.

Once verified, the beneficiaries are notified through official communication.

The bicycles are then procured and distributed to the eligible children.

The distribution of bicycles takes place at designated locations organized by the welfare board.

The timeline for the distribution of bicycles is generally set for the months of July and August each year.

This timing aligns with the beginning of the academic year in many educational institutions.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Punjab Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The board operates under the Department of Labour and Employment, Government of Punjab.

For any inquiries or assistance, beneficiaries can contact the board at their official helpline number, which is 1800 180 2040.

The board also has an official website where updates and additional information regarding the scheme can be found.

The Cycle Scheme for the Children of Construction Workers has a significant impact on the lives of beneficiaries.

It not only provides mobility but also encourages regular school attendance.

The scheme aims to reduce dropout rates among children of construction workers.

By facilitating easier access to schools, the initiative supports the educational aspirations of these children.

The government has reported that the scheme has led to an increase in school enrollment rates among targeted demographics.

Statistically, there has been a reported increase of 15% in school attendance among beneficiaries since the scheme's inception.

The initiative also promotes health and fitness among children by encouraging cycling.

The bicycles provided are designed to be durable and suitable for various terrains.

The scheme has received positive feedback from parents and educational institutions alike.

Parents have expressed gratitude for the support provided to their children.

Educational institutions have noted improved punctuality and attendance among students who received bicycles.

The government continues to monitor the implementation of the scheme to ensure it meets its objectives.

Regular assessments are conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the program.

The Cycle Scheme for the Children of Construction Workers is part of a broader strategy to uplift marginalized communities.

It aligns with the government's commitment to improving educational access for all children in India.

The scheme reflects the government's recognition of the challenges faced by construction workers and their families.

By addressing these challenges, the initiative aims to create a more equitable society.

The scheme is also an example of how targeted welfare programs can lead to significant social change.

In conclusion, the Cycle Scheme for the Children of Construction Workers is a vital welfare initiative.

It provides essential support to children from economically disadvantaged backgrounds.

The scheme not only facilitates education but also promotes overall well-being.

Through this initiative, the government aims to empower the next generation of construction workers' children.

The positive outcomes of this scheme highlight the importance of targeted welfare programs in achieving educational equity.
